newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale introduces bill to amend CWB law.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale introduces bill to amend CWB law.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale on Tuesday introduced a bill to amend the Canadian Wheat Board (CWB) Act aimed at improving the way Western Canadian wheat and barley are sold, Agriculture Canada said in a statement.

The proposed amendments should modernize the CWB's governance structure, as well as make the grain monopoly more accountable to farmers. The new legislation will also speed up cash flows to farmers and give them more power to make decisions about CWB's marketing jurisdiction.

Placing the overall management of the CWB in the hands of a board of directors with a producer majority was the strongest recommendation that Agriculture Canada had received from grain producers in Western Canada, the statement said.

"This forms the cornerstone of our amendments which we hope to have enacted well in advance of the 1997/98 crop year," Goodale said in a press release. Ottawa plans to appoint an interim CWB board of directors and expects that a final board will be elected by farmers in 1998.
The CWB, Canada's fifth largest exporter, made C$5.8 billion in wheat and barley sales in the 1995/96 crop year.
The proposed changes would give the CWB the ability to make cash purchases, expedite adjustment payments, terminate pool accounts at any time and make early payouts to farmers.

The CWB will also be allowed to issue negotiable producer certificates, defray farmers' storage and carrying costs, facilitate deliveries to condo grain storage facilities and use on-farm mobile elevators to receive deliveries.
The proposed legislation will not change the CWB's basic marketing mandate, but it will give more authority to the producer-controlled board, Agriculture Canada said.
"This policy package on grain marketing follows the most extensive consultations ever conducted in the western grains industry," said Goodale.
